As an orbital welding operator, you will work with various advanced welding processes and contribute to the production of high-quality stainless steel assemblies. Based on technical drawings and production planning, you will independently carry out work orders while ensuring precision and quality throughout the entire process.

In this role, you will prepare and process components, perform orbital and TIG welding activities, and work with technologies such as laser welding and laser marking. You will manufacture and assemble stainless steel hoses, couplings, bends, and other complex components using orbital welding heads, welding robots, and manual manipulators.

You will also be responsible for performing helium leak tests and final quality inspections to ensure all products meet the highest industry standards. In addition, you will set up and adjust machines when required and carry out first-line maintenance to support a smooth and efficient production process.

Besides the hands-on technical work, you will complete work orders digitally within the system and contribute to the development and improvement of new products and production methods. Sharing technical knowledge with colleagues and supporting team members where needed is also an important part of the role.

This is a specialized position where craftsmanship, technical expertise, precision, and quality come together within a modern high-tech production environment.

- Ability to read and interpret technical drawings
- Good command of Dutch and/or English
- Minimum mbo level 2 technical education or proven experience in metalworking
- Experience with orbital welding is a plus

As an electrical test technician, you will work full-time at a modern high-tech company in Eindhoven. You will be responsible for testing and inspecting cables, electrical modules, and smaller control cabinets. You will ensure that all products function correctly and safely before they are delivered to customers. You will work day shifts in a clean, well-organized environment where quality and precision are essential.

You will independently carry out various testing activities based on technical drawings, electrical diagrams, and test procedures. You will prepare test setups and perform safety, functional, and visual inspections. During these tests, you will check whether products meet the required quality standards and technical specifications.

When you identify defects or a​bnormalities, you will investigate their causes and carry out repairs when necessary. You will document your findings and discuss them with colleagues from the assembly department. You will also examine products returned by customers to determine the causes of any defects.

You will actively contribute ideas to improve testing and production processes. With your technical knowledge and attention to detail, you will play an important role in maintaining product quality. You will also have opportunities to further develop your skills through training and courses.

Are you technically skilled, analytical, and someone who enjoys solving problems? Apply today!

- At least 3 years of relevant experience independently testing electrical products, or a qualification in electrical engineering
- Ability to read and interpret electrical and mechanical diagrams
- Experience testing electrical modules, cables, or control cabinets
- A precise working style, strong analytical skills, and the ability to solve technical problems independently
- Good communication skills in both Dutch and English

As a maintenance technician, you will work in a large, fully automated distribution centre where technology is constantly in motion. Conveyor systems, roller conveyors, lifts and other automated installations ensure that enormous volumes of goods are moved throughout the warehouse. If a system comes to a standstill, that is where your work becomes interesting: identifying the cause of the problem and getting the system back up and running as quickly as possible.

You will work with a broad combination of mechanical engineering, electrical engineering and control technology. One fault may be caused by a mechanical component, while the next may require electrical troubleshooting or analysing the control system. You will look beyond simply replacing a faulty component: you will determine the root cause and identify what is needed to resolve the issue properly.

Using advanced monitoring applications, you can see what is happening within the system and systematically identify technical and system-related faults. You will carry out repairs and maintenance and accurately document significant breakdowns and maintenance activities.

It is precisely this combination that makes the role so interesting: rather than working on a single machine, you will work with an entire automated system in which different technologies come together. You will have the freedom to investigate faults independently, develop solutions and further expand your knowledge of control technology and PLC systems.

- You have experience analysing and resolving technical faults
- You are able to work independently, think in terms of solutions and remain calm when an installation comes to a standstill
- You have an interest in control technology; experience with PLCs is an advantage
